scope: Read-only static review of the registered six-case resource family, design/registration/source-preparation/case-map, resource contract helper, registration helper, supervisor worker/finalization/recovery, recorder attachment and resource tests. No candidate imports, compilation, tests, worker execution, raw/archive reads, registry mutations or source edits.
normal_path_assessment: Explicit v2 is frozen to 180 CPU / 190 hard CPU / 4 GiB / 360 wall. Legacy v1 remains 240 wall. Registration equality is checked before attempts; launch JSON carries v2; OS resource limits are read back; successful result assertion IDs must equal the preflight population and retain baseline IDs; recorder checks immutable registrations and per-family observed charges. Prior M reports were read only where referenced, never changed.

findings.finding: Acknowledgement resource values are compared using ordinary dict equality, without exact type validation. An acknowledgement with cpu_reservation_seconds=180.0 and wall_limit_seconds=360.0 compares equal to the expected integer-valued v2 dictionary and is accepted. This contradicts the frozen exact-type/fail-closed resource contract, although the genuine worker emits integers.
findings.repair: Validate acknowledgement and resource_limits dictionaries and exact integer field types/version before equality, retaining the explicit legacy missing-ack compatibility only. Add a float-valued acknowledgement rejection variant through result/attachment validation.

findings.finding: Recovery kills a retained process group only through candidates whose current argv exactly matches the worker command. If an acknowledged worker leader has exited but a subprocess that execs another command remains in its PGID, no candidate matches; the valid retained group is only waited on for five seconds and recovery repeatedly raises without terminating it. Long-running subprocesses can therefore strand the lifecycle despite a known worker group.
findings.repair: Use retained boot/start/group evidence to identify and safely terminate surviving members of the original group even after leader exit/exec, while preserving PID/PGID reuse guards. Add a recovery fixture with acknowledged leader gone and an exec subprocess alive; no replacement worker or new attempt may start.

findings.finding: finalize allows a durable completion with success=true/status=succeeded and result=null to bypass validate_result entirely. It checks only observed resource numbers in report.configuration, publishes the report, and marks attempts succeeded. Thus a missing result also bypasses batch-to-worker acknowledgement validation at successful finalization. Recorder later fails to attach, but the attempt and supervised receipt are already incorrectly successful and cannot be repaired through normal idempotent recovery.
findings.repair: Before any successful finish, require a non-null successful validated result and exact agreement of completion configuration/members/snapshot/worker acknowledgement with the lifecycle and retained registered trial configuration. Reject malformed success as retained failed/interrupted evidence before terminalizing. Exercise finalize/recover, not only validate_resource_binding, with missing/forged completion resource/result contracts.

findings.finding: ORCH06 tests resource helper equality and one prelaunch interruption with a synthetic incomplete registration. It never drives a successful v2 completion through finalize and record_engineering_batch, nor forged/missing v2 fields through that attachment path, nor multi-family partial finalization recovery. The case-map currently binds all final supervisor/worker/attachment agreement requirements to this method, so those registered negative and lifecycle cases are not independently asserted.
findings.repair: Extend the registered method or add explicitly mapped methods with retained synthetic successful worker/verification/lifecycle inputs, mismatched final/worker tuples, attachment rejection without ledger mutation, and two-family partial-finalization retry charging the same execution once per family. Preserve prior failed receipts and baseline report bytes.
